units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: Where is my pickle jar gone? It was kept on that same shelf for thirty whole years!

units.speaker: Sunita
units.text: Maa-ji, I did not even touch it at all. Swear on God, promise!

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: Yes yes, wings must have grown on that jar! Flew away in the night for a holy pilgrimage!

units.speaker: Neha
units.text: Hello followers! Watch live, mother-in-law versus daughter-in-law war, episode one!

units.speaker: Mahesh
units.text: <gasp> Neha, switch off the phone only! Whole neighbourhood will see it!

units.speaker: Neha
units.text: Bhaiya, whole colony is not watching. <short pause> Exactly three people are watching, yaar.

units.speaker: Golu
units.text: But my CCTV is watching everything! Everything is getting recorded!

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: Tell me, Mahesh. Who is right, your mother or your wife?

units.speaker: Mahesh
units.text: Ma... I... <laugh> Today weather is so pleasant, no?

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Stop! Order! Order!

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Enough of this daily-daily fighting! Today court will be held inside this house!

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: This steel plate is my judge's hammer. These are Dadaji's spectacles. And this sofa is the witness box!

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Dadaji went to the temple. <short pause> The court has confiscated his spectacles!

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: <laugh> Wah, Madam Judge! Today the serial is playing right at home, not on TV!

units.speaker: Golu
units.text: And I am Court CCTV in-charge! Nobody can escape from my camera!

units.speaker: Neha
units.text: Arre, this camera has a bottle cap instead of a proper lens, yaar!

units.speaker: Golu
units.text: It's not a cap, it's a zoom lens!

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Papa, whose side are you on? Mummy's side or Dadi's side?

units.speaker: Mahesh
units.text: Me? I am Switzerland only! Exactly in the middle, totally neutral!

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Then Mister Neutral, step away from the witness box. The case begins now.

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Case number one. Kamla Devi versus Sunita. Crime: vanishing a pickle jar kept safely for thirty whole years.

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: It wasn't just a jar, Madam Judge. <short pause> The taste of this entire house was in it.

units.speaker: Sunita
units.text: And I am innocent, Madam Judge. If there is proof, then bring the proof!

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Okay. The complainant will speak first. Dadi, tell us what happened last night.

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: Last night I was in the kitchen. Then she entered, and glared at my jar like a daily soap villain vamp!

units.speaker: Sunita
units.text: <laugh> This old useless jar... I will throw it away!

units.speaker: Sunita
units.text: Objection! <gasp> When do I ever laugh like that? And who makes lightning thunder in the kitchen?

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: <laugh> Objection sustained. Dadi, remove the lightning and tell the real truth.

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: <laugh> Okay, lightning didn't strike. But she did say, change this pickle jar!

units.speaker: Sunita
units.text: I said it has a crack and oil is leaking from the bottom! That is completely different!

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: And I said this jar arrived in this house before you did. That is also completely different.

units.speaker: Golu
units.text: <laugh> If both things are different-different, then why is the fight the same one?

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Next witness, Neha Bua! Come into the witness box!

units.speaker: Neha
units.text: Present! Guys, now your Neha will give witness testimony. Keep on liking, na!

units.speaker: Neha
units.text: Last night at ten o'clock I saw something... <short pause> which never even happens in TV serials, yaar!

units.speaker: Neha
units.text: Bhabhi quietly sneaked in with a huge box. Looked here, looked there, and hid it inside the cupboard!

units.speaker: Neha
units.text: And arre, here is the proof! The very same box recovered from the cupboard!

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: <gasp> A brand-new jar? Same to same like mine!

units.speaker: Golu
units.text: <gasp> Meaning fake replaced the real one! This is total Bollywood drama!

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Mummy, where did this new jar come from?

units.speaker: Sunita
units.text: <short pause> Yes, I had ordered it online. Seeing the crack on the old one.

units.speaker: Sunita
units.text: But I didn't throw the old one, Madam Judge! I thought I'd quietly swap the pickle, Maa-ji wouldn't even notice.

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: <sigh> Wouldn't even notice? <short pause> Do thirty years of memories come online now?

units.speaker: Neha
units.text: Guys, tell me in the comments, is Bhabhi guilty or not, na?

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Next witness, Papa! Do not try to run away now.

units.speaker: Mahesh
units.text: <laugh> I was just going to drink water only.

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: What did you see last night, Papa?

units.speaker: Mahesh
units.text: I saw that everyone in this house loves each other so much only.

units.speaker: Mahesh
units.text: Ma was praising Sunita, Sunita was praising Ma. And I was standing in the middle like a hero itself!

units.speaker: Neha
units.text: Arre Bhaiya, you were snoring loudly since nine o'clock last night!

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: And Mister Hero didn't even make tea for himself last night.

units.speaker: Mahesh
units.text: <gasp> Snoring is also a message of peace, no? I am not taking anyone's side!

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: <sigh> Useless witness. Please go, Mister Switzerland.

units.speaker: Golu
units.text: Judge Didi! The real proof is in my CCTV! Two o'clock recording in the night!

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: <gasp> You were awake at two o'clock at night?

units.speaker: Golu
units.text: <laugh> Had to go pee-pee. But my camera is always fully ready!

units.speaker: Neha
units.text: <laugh> Madam Judge, please write the witness's pee-pee into the court record na!

units.speaker: Golu
units.text: It was dark. Then came a ghost! White clothes, slow-slow footsteps, thud, thud, thud!

units.speaker: Golu
units.text: <gasp> The ghost took the jar and vanished! I hid inside my blanket in fear!

units.speaker: Neha
units.text: Ghost? <gasp> Ghost in the house? Guys, this will go totally viral, yaar!

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Wait. Thud, thud, thud? Did the ghost have a walking stick?

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: <laugh> Today the fan is running so slowly, no...

units.speaker: Sunita
units.text: <gasp> Ammaji... you?

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Badi Dadi, you are a senior citizen. You can give testimony from your chair itself.

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: Yes child, I took the pickle jar. <short pause> Its crack was growing bigger every day.

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: I thought, what if it breaks in Kamla's hands? So I hid it behind the Tulsi in the courtyard.

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: Then why didn't you tell me, Ammaji? <short pause> I've been screaming at Sunita since morning!

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: I got scared, Kamla. <short pause> Even at this age, I was terrified of a jar.

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Present the evidence before the court!

units.speaker: Sunita
units.text: I will bring it, Madam Judge.

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: <sigh> Thirty years ago, the day Ammaji handed over the kitchen, she placed this jar in my hands.

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: From today this jar is yours. It's the honour of this home. If it breaks, our home breaks.

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: For ten years I lived like a guest in this house. <sigh> That day, for the first time, I felt I belonged.

units.speaker: Golu
units.text: Dadi, did you look same to same like this thirty years ago too?

units.speaker: Neha
units.text: <laugh> Golu, in memories everyone appears in today's faces only, na!

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: Looked after it like a child for thirty years. With this jar, I found where I belonged.

units.speaker: Sunita
units.text: Maa-ji... <short pause> I had no idea. I was simply trying to replace a jar.

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: No, Kamla. Now listen to the whole truth.

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: <short pause> That jar is not the original.

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: <gasp> What do you mean, Ammaji?

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: Sixty years ago I was also a new bride. <sigh> My mother-in-law's real jar slipped from my hands and broke!

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: I was shaking with fear. That afternoon I ran to the market, bought the exact same jar, filled the pickle, and put it back!

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: <laugh> And till the very end, my mother-in-law never found out!

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: So the jar I worshipped for thirty years... <short pause> is just from the local market?

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: <gasp> Written at the bottom: Khurja Bazaar, two rupees!

units.speaker: Neha
units.text: <laugh> Three whole generations fighting over a two-rupee jar, yaar!

units.speaker: Mahesh
units.text: <gasp> Meaning since childhood itself I am eating bazaar pickle only?

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: <sigh> I never asked my mother-in-law why so much anger over a jar. <short pause> Just passed that fear on to you.

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: And I never asked you either, why you yourself never ate this pickle.

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: <laugh> Because every single bite reminded me of my secret theft!

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Court delivers the verdict. Dadi is guilty. Mummy is also guilty. Both committed the exact same crime!

units.speaker: Sunita
units.text: <gasp> Both? Which crime, Madam Judge?

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: You people never asked each other "why".

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Dadi never asked why Mummy wanted to change the jar. And Mummy never asked why that jar was so precious to Dadi.

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: And Badi Dadi stayed silent for sixty years. Everyone gets punishment!

units.speaker: Mahesh
units.text: <sigh> Thank God, I am saved only.

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Papa, staying quiet is also a crime. You will chop all the mangoes for the pickle!

units.speaker: Mahesh
units.text: <gasp> Whole ten kilos, is it?

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: And Dadi and Mummy together will make new pickle in the new jar. Once every day, they will ask each other, "Why?"

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: Sunita, why did you order that new jar, beta?

units.speaker: Sunita
units.text: Because you love that jar so much, Maa-ji. I just didn't want it breaking in your own hands.

units.speaker: Sunita
units.text: And what about you? Why was it so dear to you?

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: Because it made me feel part of this family.

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: From today, the new jar belongs to both of us. And even if it breaks, we will get another. The home won't break!

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: <sigh> After sixty years, my heart feels light today.

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Court is adjourned!

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: Heat mustard oil first, then let it cool down. Don't rush into it.

units.speaker: Sunita
units.text: Why, Maa-ji?

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: <laugh> Wah! Today's first "why"! Because in smoking hot oil, spices get burnt!

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: Add a little extra salt. <short pause> My mother-in-law also used to put extra.

units.speaker: Kamla
units.text: <laugh> Ammaji, now for every word of your mother-in-law, first I'll ask: why?

units.speaker: Mahesh
units.text: And today for the first time, I also picked a side! Pickle's side only!

units.speaker: Neha
units.text: Friends, mother-in-law daughter-in-law war, episode two! The Great Pickle Reunion, yaar!

units.speaker: Golu
units.text: And everything is getting recorded on CCTV!

units.speaker: Ammaji
units.text: <gasp> I didn't break it this time! See, both my hands are right here!

units.speaker: Golu
units.text: <laugh> Umm... CCTV was switched off right now.

units.speaker: Chinki
units.text: Court is back in session!
